# This is a README solely for the Bachelor Project on Reducing inference in MAS with CacheSaver

## System Construction

Most of what we have changed is the "orchestrator" folder. The folder consists of the following subfolders/files:

* pycache (irrelevant).

* experiments - Contains a file with all the code necessary to run our experiments. This is mainly running the system while logging the metrics we want to see and savingthe results in an excel file.

* orchestrated_plans - Is just a folder containing all the XML files, which are plans generated by the orchestrator.

* main - This is the main part of our extension to the implementation. There are two files "remote_orchestrator.py" and "run_mas.py", which are responsible for generating plans via the orchestrator and executing said plans respectively.

* prompts - This folder includes the prompts that were used for the orchestrator. There are prompts for the orchestrator having access to all sub-agents as well as only each agent individually.

* results - This folder contains the results from our experiments in the form of excel files and the cache.db files used for each experiment.

* setup - Contains a "setup.md" file, which explains how to setup the docker image/container and the uv environment necessary to actually run the code.

* utils - Includes a "utils.py" file, which contains some utility functions like calculating cost per token.


## Adding CacheSaver

These changes were mostly to the samplers, which are how the agents in the execution part interact with the LLM. We added samplers for using OpenAI with CacheSaver as well as using Groq with and without CacheSaver. The orchestrator talks directly to the LLM however, so we just added CacheSaver in the "remote_orchestrator.py" file directly.


## Running the code

AS stated above, there is a setup markdown file in the "orchestrator" folder detailing how to setup a Docker image and a uv environment in order to run the code. The Docker image is about 12 gb and uv env is somewhere between 5-10 gb approximately.
